recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一個大型巨噬細胞的細胞質內有多個 2–4 µm 小型卵圓形酵母菌，菌體中央有深染的核質、周圍有透明暈圈，同時可見被吞噬的紅血球，符合組織漿菌症造成的全血球減少。
features: Large macrophage with abundant vacuolated gray-blue cytoplasm and an eccentric nucleus with coarse chromatin
Multiple small (approximately 2–4 µm), uniform, oval intracellular yeasts each surrounded by a clear halo
Yeasts with a central or polar basophilic dot/crescent of cytoplasm; no kinetoplast
Phagocytosed red cell/erythroid remnant within the macrophage cytoplasm (hemophagocytosis)
Additional small dark intracytoplasmic fragments; surrounding red cells and a nucleated cell at the lower edge
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a large macrophage with abundant vacuolated cytoplasm containing numerous small, uniform, oval yeast forms, each with a basophilic center and a surrounding clear halo, together with a phagocytosed red cell. No kinetoplasts are seen, distinguishing the organisms from Leishmania amastigotes. Findings are consistent with Histoplasma capsulatum infection of the marrow with associated hemophagocytosis, explaining the pancytopenia; confirmation by GMS/PAS stain, culture or Histoplasma antigen testing is recommended.

ddx.vs: Leishmania amastigotes contain a nucleus and a separate bar-shaped kinetoplast without a surrounding halo or PAS/GMS-positive cell wall.
Talaromyces yeasts show central septation from binary fission and elongated forms rather than budding oval yeasts with halos.
Candida glabrata is slightly larger, less consistently intracellular and grows rapidly in routine culture without the endemic exposure history.
Toxoplasma bradyzoites are crescent-shaped with a central nucleus and PAS-negative walls, lacking clear halos.
